note: Craft, building and scholarship technologies (the tables of section 4 of the spec), the gate technologies (3.4), the folder and category tables (2) and the AI research focuses (2.3). Technology keys are written without the zin_tech_ prefix (the loader adds it). Warfare's rows are in technologies_warfare.json. Names avoid the words of banned_words.json (the key of a row may still say steel or mortar; the player never reads a key).

folders.name: Arms and Armour
folders.desc: The smith's and the armourer's trades: blades, bows, mail, and the drills that make them count.

folders.name: Mounts and Kin
folders.desc: Horses, camels and the great kin: what carries a host to battle and what outweighs it when it arrives.

folders.name: Engines and Walls
folders.desc: Throwing engines and bolt-throwers, and the walls and harbour chains that answer them.

folders.name: Lore and Wards
folders.desc: Healers' craft, wardsong and hallowed arms, and the dark rites kept in the south.

folders.name: Camp and Road
folders.desc: Scouts, sappers, wagons and the stores that let a host march a season.

folders.name: Galleys and Warships
folders.desc: Hulls, oars and sails, and the harbours that feed them.

folders.name: Eyries
folders.desc: The lore of the winged: dragon keeping and, where the beasts are bred, griffin riding.

folders.name: Craft and Works
folders.desc: Stone, ore, forge and field: the trades that build a realm and feed it.

folders.name: Letters and Beacons
folders.desc: Scriptoria, seals and beacon towers: how a realm reads, writes and keeps watch.

folders.name: Doctrine of the Host
folders.desc: How the hosts of a realm are taught to stand, march and break.

folders.name: Doctrine of the Sea
folders.desc: How the fleets of a realm are taught to row, sail and board.

folders.name: Doctrine of the Winged
folders.desc: How the winged are taught to hunt, scout and strike.

folders.name: Hidden Doctrine
folders.desc: Held in reserve. Nothing of this folder is shown.

technologies.name: Dressed Stone
technologies.desc: Masons learn to square and fit their blocks, so walls rise straight and halls stand longer. Building goes faster and repairs come cheaper.

technologies.name: Slaked Lime
technologies.desc: Burnt lime, slaked in pits and mixed with sand, binds a wall into one stone. Building and repair go faster again.

technologies.name: Arch and Vault
technologies.desc: Masons roof wide halls and bridge deep gorges with a ring of wedged stones. Larger works go up in less time.

technologies.name: Masons' Lodges
technologies.desc: Masons band into lodges that keep their secrets, teach their sons and travel to wherever a great work is begun.

technologies.name: Great Scaffolds
technologies.desc: Timber frames climb as high as the stone does, and the work no longer waits on the weather.

technologies.name: Pit Props
technologies.desc: Timber props hold the roof of a shaft, and miners follow the iron seam deeper than before.

technologies.name: Quarry Wedges
technologies.desc: Iron wedges and wet wood split the rock along its grain. Quarries give more stone for less sweat.

technologies.name: Drainage Wheels
technologies.desc: Wheels of buckets lift water out of the deep workings, and the gold-bearing veins can be followed below the springs.

technologies.name: Deep Shafts
technologies.desc: Shafts sink past the old workings into untouched rock, braced and aired by those who have learned how.

technologies.name: Assayers' Rolls
technologies.desc: Assayers keep rolls of every seam they have tested, so no miner digs where the rock has already been proved poor.

technologies.name: Water-Wheels
technologies.desc: A river turns the bellows and the grindstones, and the guild workshops make more with the same hands.

technologies.name: Trip-Hammers
technologies.desc: A cam lifts a heavy hammer and lets it fall, over and over, while the smith turns the iron.

technologies.name: Standard Patterns
technologies.desc: Guilds agree on one pattern for each piece, so parts made in different workshops fit together and a changed order costs less.

technologies.name: Many Hands
technologies.desc: Each worker learns one step of the making and does it all day. The work is quicker, and the apprentices learn faster.

technologies.name: Pattern Books
technologies.desc: Every pattern is drawn and kept in a book, so a workshop can turn from one making to another without losing a week. It shuts out the Masters' Benches.

technologies.name: Masters' Benches
technologies.desc: The best hands keep their benches and teach whoever sits beside them, and a new workshop reaches full skill sooner. It shuts out the Pattern Books.

technologies.name: Seed Reserves
technologies.desc: Sealed stone granaries hold seed against a bad year, so one failed harvest no longer empties the realm's provisions.

technologies.name: Irrigation Canals
technologies.desc: Canals carry the spring flood to dry fields. Harvests swell, and villages grow where hunger once held them back.

technologies.name: Great Halls
technologies.desc: The guilds gather their forges and benches under one great roof, where a hundred smiths share a fire. It shuts out the Village Forges.

technologies.name: Vaulted Halls
technologies.desc: Stone vaults roof the halls wider than timber ever could, with room for more benches and more fires.

technologies.name: Covered Yards
technologies.desc: Roofs over the shipways and the timber yards let the work go on through rain and snow.

technologies.name: Treadwheel Cranes
technologies.desc: Men walking inside great wheels lift beams and anvils that no gang of porters could raise.

technologies.name: Crown Foundries
technologies.desc: The crown raises vast foundries under its own seal, and the greatest castings of the age are poured there.

technologies.name: Village Forges
technologies.desc: A forge in every village and a smith in every forge: the work is spread wide and can turn to any need. It shuts out the Great Halls.

technologies.name: Roadside Smithies
technologies.desc: Smithies beside the high roads mend wagons and tools on the spot, and the work never waits for a distant guild.

technologies.name: Charcoal-Burners' Leagues
technologies.desc: The woodland burners bind themselves into leagues and promise every forge its charcoal on a fixed day.

technologies.name: Travelling Smiths
technologies.desc: Smiths with a cart, an anvil and a charter go where the need is, and the realm's best hands are never idle.

technologies.name: Steading Foundries
technologies.desc: Even a small steading raises a foundry of its own, and no single fire holds the realm's whole craft.

technologies.name: Slipways
technologies.desc: Greased slipways of stone and timber let a hull be laid down, built and launched without a single wasted tide.

technologies.name: Dry Docks
technologies.desc: A basin with a sea-gate takes a ship in, is pumped dry, and leaves the hull open to the shipwright's tools.

technologies.name: Great Yards
technologies.desc: Whole shipyards are planned as one work, with ropewalks, sawpits and berths side by side.

technologies.name: Wellspring Tapping
technologies.desc: At the known wells, careful hands draw Essence into sealed jars. The work is slow, local and never done alone.

technologies.name: Ley-Stone Channels
technologies.desc: Channels cut into the old stones guide the Essence to where it can be gathered, and little is lost on the way.

technologies.name: Phials and Vials
technologies.desc: Sealed phials of warded glass let Essence be kept and carried, and a realm can lay some by for hard times.

technologies.name: Deep Wells
technologies.desc: The learned of the Great Library chart where the wells run deepest, and the boldest sink shafts to them.

technologies.name: Leaf-Craft
technologies.desc: The elves coax living wood into the shapes they need, and the forest gives its timber without a tree falling.

technologies.name: Forge-Pits
technologies.desc: Orcs and trolls dig their forges into the hillside and feed them day and night. What comes out is rough and plentiful.

technologies.name: Quarry-Songs
technologies.desc: Giants sing to the rock until it breaks along the line they want, and their quarries give stone in great clean blocks.

technologies.name: Vent-Forges
technologies.desc: In the Dead Lands the hot vents of the earth feed forges that never go cold, and Essence rises with the fumes.

technologies.name: Scriptoria
technologies.desc: Scribes copy the records of the realm in warm rooms, and what one scholar learns no longer dies with him.

technologies.name: Libraries
technologies.desc: The copied books are gathered, shelved and catalogued, and a scholar can find in an hour what once took a year.

technologies.name: Universities
technologies.desc: Masters and students dwell together under a charter, and learning is taught, disputed and handed on in the open.

technologies.name: Scholars' Conclaves
technologies.desc: The learned of many halls meet each year to read their findings aloud, and each leaves with the others' work.

technologies.name: The Great Library
technologies.desc: One vast house holds every book the realm can gather. When the shelves are full, another chair is set for a scholar to work in.

technologies.name: Wax Seals
technologies.desc: A letter closed with a signet and wax cannot be opened without showing it. Couriers and clerks learn to trust the mark.

technologies.name: Cipher Scripts
technologies.desc: Scribes agree on secret alphabets, so that a stolen letter is only a page of nonsense.

technologies.name: Sealed Couriers
technologies.desc: Sworn riders carry sealed pouches by relays of fresh horses, and never read what they carry.

technologies.name: Cipher Wheels
technologies.desc: Turning bronze wheels, a patient clerk can try a thousand keys against a stolen letter before supper.

technologies.name: Letter Counts
technologies.desc: Scholars count how often each letter appears in a secret page, and the commonest signs give themselves away.

technologies.name: Reading Rooms
technologies.desc: A locked chamber where trained readers work through every captured letter, and nothing that passes through it is forgotten.

technologies.name: Watch Fires
technologies.desc: A pile of dry wood on every headland, tended night and day. When a sail is seen the next fire is lit, and the word runs down the coast.

technologies.name: Horn Chains
technologies.desc: Horns on every hilltop answer one another from tower to tower, and a warning crosses a province before a rider could mount.

technologies.name: Far-Seeing Glass
technologies.desc: Ground lenses in brass tubes bring distant hulls close, and the watchers on the towers see a fleet hours before it lands.

technologies.name: Glass Towers
technologies.desc: Tall towers crowned with great lenses and signal lamps watch the whole horizon, and no coast is left unwatched.

gates.name: The First Sealed Work
gates.desc: No craft of Erdae reaches this work. It is kept shut, and nothing researches it.
